match.reason: None of the bank points covers acid rain, dissolved carbon dioxide or ocean acidity; they teach acid reactions, acid strength, Ka, functional groups and buffers, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Acid rain and ocean acidity
card: Carbon dioxide in the air dissolves in rain and forms carbonic acid, a weak acid. This makes unpolluted rain naturally slightly acidic, with a pH a little below 7.
Burning fuels and smelting metals release sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. These dissolve in water to form stronger acids, so acid rain has a lower pH than natural rain.
The ocean is slightly basic. It absorbs carbon dioxide from the air, and the carbonic acid formed lowers the pH of seawater.
More carbon dioxide in the air means more is absorbed, so the ocean becomes less basic. Its pH falls towards 7, which is called ocean acidification.
draft.remember: Carbon dioxide makes rain slightly acidic. Pollutant gases make stronger acid rain, and extra carbon dioxide makes the ocean less basic.

a.q: Why is unpolluted rain slightly acidic?
opts: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid
Dissolved sulfur dioxide forms sulfuric acid
Dissolved nitrogen oxides form nitric acid
Dissolved oxygen forms a weak acid in the rain
a.why: Carbon dioxide occurs naturally in air and dissolves in rain to form carbonic acid. Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides mostly come from pollution, so they explain acid rain, not natural rain.
a.clue: Think of the gas that is in air without any pollution.

b.q: Air carbon dioxide levels rise near Hobart. What is the likely effect on the nearby ocean water?
opts: Its pH falls, so it becomes less basic
Its pH rises, so it becomes more basic
Its pH stays the same, as the ocean is basic
Its pH falls below 7 at once, so it turns acidic
b.why: More carbon dioxide in the air means more dissolves in seawater and forms carbonic acid. This lowers the pH, so the ocean becomes less basic. The pH falls towards 7 and does not turn acidic at once.
b.clue: More dissolved carbon dioxide means more carbonic acid.

a.best: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid

b.best: Its pH falls, so it becomes less basic

problems.detail: The setting 'Air carbon dioxide levels rise near Hobart' suggests a local effect on nearby seawater. Carbon dioxide mixes through the whole atmosphere and ocean acidification is a global change, so the local framing could mislead. A general stem such as 'Carbon dioxide levels in the air rise' would be clearer.
